# app-tokens read

Command: `boundary app-tokens read`

The `app-tokens read` command reads an app token given its ID.

## Examples

The following example reads the app token details for an app token with the ID `appt_1234567890`.

```shell-session
$ boundary app-tokens read -id appt_1234567890
```

**Example output:**

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```plaintext
App Token information:
  Approximate Last Access Time:   Thu, 01 Oct 2026 18:04:09 PDT
  Created By User ID:             u_1234567890
  Created Time:                   Thu, 01 Oct 2026 18:04:09 PDT
  Description:                    An example app token in the global scope.
  Expiration Time:                Sat, 31 Oct 2026 18:04:09 PDT
  ID:                             appt_1234567890
  Name:                           Example App Token
  Status:                         active

  Scope:
    ID:                           global
    Name:                         global
    Type:                         global

  Permissions:
    Permission 1:
      Grants:
        id=*;type=target;actions=list,read
      Grant Scopes:
        this

  Authorized Actions:
    read
    read:self
    revoke
    delete
    no-op
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

## Usage

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```shell-session
$ boundary app-tokens read [options] [args]
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

### Command options

- `-id` `(string: "")` - The ID of the app token to read.
